newsitem.title: FRANCE: Le Monde details Juppe warning to govt on deficit.
newsitem.headline: Le Monde details Juppe warning to govt on deficit.

text.p: Former French Prime Minister Alain Juppe warned the new Socialist-led government that it would have to take tough action to prevent the public deficit rising above four percent of gross domestic product next year, afternoon daily Le Monde said on Thursday.
It quoted Juppe as saying in a letter the public deficit could however still be reduced to three percent next year.

"The initial work on the budget outlook carried out by the budget ministry experts suggest a trend in public deficits to a figure above four percent of GDP, based, it is true, on particularly low forecasts for revenues," Le Monde quoted Juppe's letter as saying.
"This figure could be reduced to three percent after savings on budget and welfare spending, questioning some fiscal spending and tapping exceptional non-fiscal revenues," it said.
It said that Juppe had warned that economic growth was not having a strong enough effect on government and welfare revenues to allow the deficit to fall spontaneously.

"It is therefore certain that the credible presentation next September of a budget bill and social security bill showing a deficit of three percent will require a very strong political commitment from the whole government to limit the burden which public spending makes on our country," the letter said.
It said Juppe told the incoming government in the letter, dated June 2, that his government had begun the task of reducing budget deficits and the outlook for growth and jobs was good.
But he said further measures would be needed to reduce the public deficit this year to three percent of GDP.
He said revenues were some 35 billion francs less than expected. This would correspond to an overshooting of slightly over 0.4 percentage points of GDP, Le Monde said.
A decision to spend a 10 billion franc surplus in national unemployment fund UNEDIC, otherwise earmarked for the budget, would add slightly more than 0.1 percentage points of GDP.
New public spending needs may for an amount of around eight billion francs -- slightly less than 0.1 percentage points of GDP -- though savings were planned to offset this.
The figures given in Le Monde for the 1997 deficit are in line with expectations that an audit of public finances due on July 21 will show a deficit between 3.4 percent and 3.8 percent of GDP.
The government has said it will take action to curb the deficit, depending on the results of the audit.
Financial daily La Tribune said earlier that the audit was likely to forecast the deficit at 3.6 to 3.7 percent of GDP.

Le Monde also quoted Juppe as saying the welfare accounts -- which are run separately from the central government budget -- were unlikely to show a deficit much more than five billion more than the 30 billion initially forecast.
